verdict.rationale: Bun's own docs cover all three operations as CLI commands. `bun add` writes the package to the chosen dependency group in package.json (with `--exact` and `--catalog` options), `bun remove` strips it from every dependency group and updates bun.lock, and `bun update` / `bun up` upgrades dependencies within their ranges, with an interactive mode and targeted nested updates. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that `bun add` updates bun.lock, any statement about safe or atomic rewrites, and independent hands-on corroboration of manifest and lockfile rewriting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can add, remove, and upgrade dependencies through CLI commands that safely rewrite the manifest and lockfile, so an agent never hand-edits them

citations.quote: Bun writes the package to `dependencies` unless you pass `--dev`, `--optional`, or `--peer`.
Bun removes the package from every dependency group in `package.json` that lists it and updates `bun.lock`.
`bun update` (alias `bun up`) updates every dependency, direct and transitive, to the newest version allowed by the ranges that request it.
Bun writes the exact version number to your `package.json` instead of a version range.
